WORKING TOGETHER FOR UPHOLDING HUMAN DIGNITY IN OUR NATION
 
A Communiqué issued at the end of the Second Plenary Meeting of the Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria (CBCN) held at Our Lady and St. Kizito Pastoral Centre, Oke-Gada, Ede, Osogbo Diocese, Osun State, 10 - 18 September 2026
 
1. PREAMBLE
We, the Catholic Bishops of Nigeria, held our Second Plenary Meeting for the year at the Our Lady and St. Kizito Pastoral Centre, Oke-Gada, Ede, Osogbo Diocese, Osun State, from 10 to 18 September 2026. Having prayerfully deliberated on issues affecting the Church and the Nigerian State, we issue this Communiqué:
 
2. THE DIGNITY OF THE HUMAN PERSON
We commend the Holy Father, Pope Leo XIV, for his recent encyclical Magnifica Humanitas (On safeguarding the Human Person), and we invite all to study this momentous document. Dignity of the human person is an inalienable gift rooted in being created in the image and likeness of God (Genesis 1:27). It is intrinsic, unconditional, and inviolable, grounded not in what a person can do, achieve, or contribute, but in who he or she is (Magnifica Humanitas, 53, 55). For this reason, the recognition of human dignity and the right to life lies at the foundation of Catholic Social Teaching. They are a prerequisite for pursuing all its other principles, including the common good and social justice.
 
Sexual and other forms of violence are instances of the abuse of the dignity of the human person. The Catholic Church opposes every form of violence and abuse. Sacred Scripture teaches that God created the human person, male and female, equal in dignity and called them to relationships marked by love, fidelity, and mutual respect. We reaffirm that violence and abuse contradict this divine purpose. Every human person possesses an inviolable dignity. Sexual and other forms of abuse violate this dignity and leave deep wounds in those who suffer it (Dignitas Infinita, 1, 43-45). We acknowledge that the credibility of our pastoral witness is strongly impacted by how the Church responds to abuse, defends the weak, and listens to those who suffer. We urge our people in the Church and Society to avoid all forms of abuse and violence, and respect the dignity of the human person, male and female.
 
3. THE CHURCH AND TECHNOLOGY
Technology is a profoundly human reality, linked to the autonomy and freedom of man. We express and confirm the primacy of the spiritual over the material even in the use of technology. Technology is not inherently evil or antagonistic to humanity, but it is never neutral (Magnifica Humanitas 4, 9, 16). As a vehicle for evangelization, we enjoin all to use it to transform data into knowledge and insights for greater value. We urge all politicians and others to exercise responsibility and ethics in deploying technology and Artificial Intelligence (AI), especially as we approach the forthcoming elections.
 
4. CONTINUED NEO-PAGANISM IN OUR NATION
We have continued to witness the challenge of neo-paganism in our nation. As we have previously noted, this attitude involves a growing trend where believers and especially youths return to idle worship, due largely to economic hardships, cultural revival, and shallow Christian formation. Since modern neo-paganism spreads rapidly through internet culture, media engagement, and books, we encourage pastoral agents to intentionally incorporate the use of digital spaces, social media, and online catechesis in teaching the truth of the Gospel. We recommend a healthy inculturation which seeks to respect our positive cultural heritage while firmly upholding foundational Christian truths.

Everyone already understands that someday artificial intelligence may become powerful enough to surpass human intelligence. But for now, it has managed to provoke a prolonged and bitter battle inside Trump’s White House.

According to The Wall Street Journal, White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have spent months meeting almost daily with administration officials who are concerned that AI is developing at breakneck speed without adequate safeguards.

Opposing them is Trump’s technology adviser David Sacks, who has strongly resisted additional government regulation.

The conflict intensified after Sacks, in a last-minute phone call, reportedly persuaded the easily swayed Trump not to sign a planned executive order that would have tightened oversight of new AI models. Wiles and Bessent pushed back and ultimately convinced Trump to sign a significantly watered-down version instead.

But the fight is far from over. Wiles and Bessent, who are pushing for stronger safety measures, have been joined by National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross. Sacks, meanwhile, argues that AI companies themselves should be responsible for the safety of their products and held accountable when things go wrong, but that creating an entirely new federal regulatory system is unnecessary.

In this battle, Sacks also has powerful allies in the private sector. Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang have urged Trump not to impose tough restrictions. Along with Elon Musk, they have also opposed plans to create an industry-funded regulatory body for AI.

And then there is Trump himself.

While senior officials in his administration argue over how much government oversight this rapidly developing technology actually needs, Trump announced on Monday that he had already identified the most important “safeguard”:

“The only control or ‘guardrails’ AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (high IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S. has one — in abundance!”

Trump went even further, dismissing fears that AI could eventually “take over the world and destroy humanity” as a “hoax.” His argument is that restricting AI development in the United States could allow China to overtake America.

That is what makes this battle inside Trump’s White House so important. Wiles and Bessent are pushing for stronger safeguards. Sacks argues that developers can police their own products without another federal regulator. And some of the most powerful figures in the technology industry are fighting additional oversight as well.

Trump, however, has proposed a third approach: apparently, everything revolves around him — the great and mighty one.

“Me… me… me…” 🤦‍♀️

Or, as the wonderfully crude Russian expression goes: “Я… я… — хуй от муравья.”
